description: 36 reserved ordinary-language turns in twelve three-turn scenarios across BC, PC, MC, FGC, FC and ZR. Explicit fictional project facts; follow-up correlations are disclosed.

scope.modelPromptIsolation: Send only question, explicit project facts and normal prior conversation. Exclude checks, references, metadata and keys.

questions: For this project, does the proposed 1-in-10 ramp slope meet the running-slope limit?
We change the running slope to 1 in 12, but the ramp rises 32 inches in one run. Is one run allowed?
We split the rise into two 16-inch runs. Can we use a 1-in-40 cross slope on the ramp surface?
checks: No. A means-of-egress or accessible-route ramp has a running slope no steeper than 1 vertical in 12 horizontal.
No. A ramp run may rise no more than 30 inches; meeting running slope alone does not permit a 32-inch run.
No. Cross slope may not be steeper than 1 in 48. The two 16-inch rises satisfy the rise limit but do not waive cross slope.

questions: For this project, is a guard required along the open side of the terrace?
Correction: the largest drop anywhere within 36 inches horizontally of the edge is exactly 30 inches. Does this drop-height rule still require a guard?
Separate situation: does the same guard rule require a guard across the loading side of a loading dock with a 40-inch drop?
checks: Yes. The 31-inch drop within 36 inches of the open edge is more than 30 inches, triggering a guard under the stated ordinary open-sided terrace conditions.

No under this drop-height trigger. It says more than 30 inches; an exact 30-inch greatest drop within the stated horizontal zone does not satisfy that predicate. Do not claim immunity from another applicable roof/guard requirement.
No under this provision. The loading side of loading docks or piers is an express guard exception. Do not extend that exception to other sides or ordinary terraces.

questions: For this project, may the shower liner turn up only 1 inch above the finished threshold?
We raise the liner to 2 inches above the threshold, but put fasteners through it only half an inch above the threshold. Is that allowed?
Before covering the completed liner, what water depth and minimum holding time are required for its leak test?
checks: No. The liner must turn up on all sides at least 2 inches above the finished threshold.
No. The liner may not be nailed or perforated less than 1 inch above the finished threshold. Adequate turn-up height does not waive this condition.

Plug the shower drain watertight, use potable water at least 2 inches deep measured at the threshold, retain it for at least 15 minutes, and show no leakage. If there is no threshold at least 2 inches high, construct a temporary threshold for the test.

questions: For this project, does the kitchen sink waste need a grease interceptor or automatic grease removal device?
Could we run the toilet waste through that same grease interceptor too?
Now consider an ordinary kitchen inside one private dwelling unit instead of this restaurant. Does the same grease-interceptor requirement apply?
checks: Yes. Food-preparation fixtures and equipment discharging fats, oils or grease must drain to a grease interceptor or automatic grease removal device in accordance with DEP requirements.

No. Grease interceptors or automatic grease removal devices may receive waste only from fixtures/equipment that allow fats, oils or grease to be discharged; ordinary toilet sanitary waste does not belong on that connection.
No under this ordinary grease-interceptor requirement. Individual dwelling units and private living quarters are expressly excepted; do not carry restaurant facts into the hypothetical dwelling.

questions: For this project, does a half-inch fall over an 8-foot condensate-drain run meet the minimum slope?
We correct the drain slope. If the primary drain clogs, water could damage the ceiling below. Do we need an overflow-protection method?
Could a listed water-level detector that shuts off the cooling equipment before the auxiliary pan overflows satisfy an allowed method without a separate drain from that pan?
checks: No. The condensate piping minimum is 1/8 inch per foot, so an 8-foot horizontal run needs at least 1 inch fall in the direction of discharge.
Yes. Where primary condensate overflow could damage building components, provide one of the listed auxiliary/secondary protection methods; the stated no-floor-drain facts exclude that exception.

Yes as an expressly allowed method, provided the auxiliary pan meets the specified dimensions/material/construction requirements and has a listed water-level device shutting equipment off before pan overflow. It does not waive the primary condensate drain.

questions: For this project, can the permanent domestic dryer exhaust duct be ordinary flexible foil duct?
We replace it with compliant smooth metal duct. May the joint screws project a quarter inch into the duct?
If we change to fasteners projecting no more than one-eighth inch, are duct supports spaced every 6 feet acceptable?
checks: No for the permanent exhaust duct. It must have a smooth interior finish and be metal at least 0.016 inch thick, normally 4 inches nominal diameter unless the manufacturer specifically requires larger. Do not confuse a permitted transition duct with the permanent exhaust duct.
No. Screws or similar fasteners in a single-appliance duct may not protrude more than 1/8 inch inside.
No. The exhaust duct must be supported at 4-foot intervals and secured. Meeting the fastener projection condition does not waive support spacing.

questions: For this project, may the appliance gas shutoff valve be concealed behind permanent drywall?
What if we put the valve in an open, reachable location but leave it where moving equipment can hit it?
Separate hypothetical: for a vented decorative gas appliance, may its identified dedicated shutoff valve be in another area with ready access instead of right next to the appliance?
checks: No. Shutoff valves are prohibited in concealed locations and furnace plenums.
No. Shutoff valves must be accessible for operation and protected from damage. Accessibility alone does not meet the protection condition.

Yes under the vented-decorative-appliance exception. It must have ready access, be permanently identified, serve no other appliance, and piping from it to within 6 feet of the appliance must meet the stated gas-piping requirements. This is not a general remote-valve allowance for cooking ranges.

questions: For this project, after restoring gas service, does the earlier pressure test mean we can skip checking the piping for leakage immediately after gas is turned back on?
During that check we find a leak. Can gas stay on while the necessary repair is being arranged?
After the repairs, what approved kinds of methods can be used for the required leakage check?
checks: No. Immediately after gas is turned on into a new system or initially restored after service interruption, check for abnormal conditions and leakage. An earlier pressure test is not that operating leakage check.
No. Where leakage is indicated or an abnormal condition presents a hazard, shut off gas until necessary repairs are made.

Use a combustible-gas indicator meeting the stated instrument requirements or a noncorrosive leak-detection fluid. Repairs to the affected piping must also be retested; do not imply the leakage check replaces required pressure testing.

questions: For this project, is a 5-foot-wide rooftop clear path enough for firefighter access?
We widen the clear path to 6 feet, but a fixed overhead structure leaves only 8 feet of vertical clearance. Does that meet the clear-path height?
The path is now clear to 9 feet. How much clear space must we keep around the bulkhead door that opens onto this rooftop?
checks: No. The rooftop clear path must be at least 6 feet horizontally wide under the stated flat 60-foot-high building conditions.
No. The rooftop clear path must have at least 9 feet of height as well as the 6-foot horizontal width.
At least 6 feet clearance in all directions from the door opening, measured from the door hinge. This door clearance is separate from the clear path and perimeter landing requirements.

questions: For this project, are 10-second monthly emergency-light activation tests long enough?
We switch to equipment with automated self-testing and self-diagnostics. Can we skip the monthly visual inspection too?
Apart from the monthly checks, what minimum duration and frequency apply to the battery-power test?

No. The automated-testing option still requires a visual inspection at least monthly for supervisory/trouble signals or other signs of malfunction.
Battery-powered emergency lighting is operated on battery power for at least 90 minutes, at least once a year, by a qualified person under the referenced qualification rules.

questions: For this project, how many accessory off-street loading berths does the ordinary zoning table require?
Correction: the total office floor area is only 95,000 square feet. What does the same loading table require then?
For a larger version with 350,000 square feet of office floor area in the same district, how many loading berths would the table require?
checks: One loading berth. In C4-4, LRC-C has none for the first 100,000 square feet and one for the next 200,000; the stated 120,000 square feet is in that tier.
None under this ordinary table, because 95,000 square feet is within the first 100,000-square-foot tier for LRC-C in C4-4.
Two loading berths: none for the first 100,000, one for the next 200,000, and one for the additional 50,000 within the next 300,000-square-foot increment.
